page: Microsoft Azure E32-8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained-core configuration designed for memory-intensive workloads that require lower compute licensing overhead. The instance allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is provisioned with 256 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI and BF16, hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no local storage and no bundled GPUs, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistent storage.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance. The AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivers top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests as well as single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core throughput and overall PassMark metrics reflect expected constraints from its 8 vCPU cap, placing multi-threaded execution within the middle tier. Memory benchmarks indicate 50.05 GB/s uncached large-block read throughput and 34.01 GB/s write throughput. In application-level testing, the instance achieved 14.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 15.51 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural trade-off of the E32-8as_v7 is its intentional compute constraint relative to total RAM. By capping available compute to 8 vCPUs while preserving the 256 GB memory footprint of an E32-class footprint, the instance enables qualitative cost efficiencies for software licensed per core. It is well matched for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, memory-bound analytics, and enterprise data workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for high-memory workloads with constrained CPU requirements. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, the instance provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and pairs them with 256 GB of RAM, yielding 32 GB per vCPU. It features AVX-512 support, 32 MB of L3 cache, and dedicated core allocation under Microsoft Hyper-V. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Performance evaluation reveals top-tier single-threaded capability in compression and stress-ng benchmarks, while multi-core metrics and uncached memory throughput perform in the median tier. With 14.19 million Redis SET operations per second, this configuration is positioned for memory-intensive enterprise software, large in-memory caches, and databases seeking to minimize per-core licensing expenses.
